ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a 3×3 grid: the upper-left cell is 20, the upper-middle cell is 1, the middle-right cell is a question mark, and the remaining cells are empty. The problem asks to fill it with 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100, so that the products of every row, every column, and the two diagonals are all the same. Write each number as an exponent pair of 2^a5^b: (1,2,4,5,10,20,25,50,100) respectively correspond to (0,0),(1,0),(2,0),(0,1),(1,1),(2,1),(0,2),(1,2),(2,2), that is, a,b both take all combinations of 0,1,2. Equal products are equivalent to the sums of the exponent pairs on each line being the same. The total exponent sum of each coordinate is 0+1+2 repeated three times, that is 9, so the exponent sum of each row or each column must be 3; the target exponent sum of each line is (3,3). The top row already has 20 and 1, that is (2,1)+(0,0), so the upper-right cell must be (3,3)-(2,1)-(0,0)=(1,2), corresponding to 50. The center of a 3×3 additive magic square must be the average exponent pair (1,1), so the center is 10. The sum of the exponent pairs of two cells opposite across the center is (2,2), therefore the lower-left cell opposite the upper-right cell (1,2) is (1,0), corresponding to 2. Look again at the left column: upper-left (2,1), lower-left (1,0), so the middle-left cell is (3,3)-(2,1)-(1,0)=(0,2), corresponding to 25. The middle-left cell and the middle-right cell are opposite across the center, and the sum of the two is (2,2), so the middle-right question-mark cell is (2,2)-(0,2)=(2,0), corresponding to 4.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a 3 by 3 square with 20 in the top-left cell, 1 in the top-middle cell, and the question mark in the middle-right cell. From the text, use the allowed numbers 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100 and the rule that every row, column, and diagonal has the same product. Convert each number to its prime-exponent pair in the form 2^a 5^b: the nine numbers correspond to all pairs (a,b) with a,b in {0,1,2}. Equal products then become equal sums of exponent pairs, so this is an additive magic-square problem in two coordinates. The total exponent sum in each coordinate is 9, so every line has exponent sum 3. The top row has (20,1,top-right) = (2,1)+(0,0)+?, forcing the top-right pair to be (1,2), i.e. 50. In any 3 by 3 additive magic square with line sum 3, the center coordinate must be 1 in each prime dimension, so the center is (1,1)=10. Then the opposite cells relative to the center must have exponent-pair sums (2,2). Use the diagonal and column constraints to determine bottom-left = 2, middle-left = 25, and therefore the middle-right question-mark cell is (2,0)=4.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a 3 by 3 multiplication magic square with 20 in the top-left cell, 1 in the top-middle cell, and the question mark in the middle-right cell. From the text, multiply all nine available numbers: their total product is 10^9, so if the common line product is M, then M^3 = 10^9 because the three rows together contain all nine entries. Hence M = 1000. The top row then gives 20 · 1 · top-right = 1000, so the top-right cell is 50. In a 3 by 3 multiplicative magic square, the center must satisfy center^3 = M, so the center is 10. Therefore each pair of opposite cells around the center must multiply to M/center = 100. Since top-left is 20, bottom-right is 5; since top-right is 50, bottom-left is 2. Now use the first column: 20 · middle-left · 2 = 1000, so middle-left = 25. Finally the middle row product gives 25 · 10 · ? = 1000, hence ? = 4.
